title: Leveraging Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation to Support Learners’ Understanding of Knowledge Concepts in MOOCs
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the challenge that learners in Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) often lack direct instructor interaction and may struggle to understand new knowledge concepts. While learners increasingly use large language models (LLMs) for support, the authors note that standard LLMs can hallucinate and that existing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems in education are limited by unstructured course materials and by requiring learners to formulate their own questions without guidance.

To address this, the authors propose a Graph RAG pipeline implemented in the MOOC platform CourseMapper. The approach combines Educational Knowledge Graphs (EduKGs), which structure course concepts and related Wikipedia resources, with Personal Knowledge Graphs (PKGs), which model each learner’s “did not understand” concepts. The system has two main components: a PKG-based question generation method that recommends personalized questions about concepts a learner does not understand, and an EduKG-based question answering method that retrieves graph-structured evidence and generates cited answers. The pipeline also includes graph-based reranking of generated questions and citation/highlighting of answer sources.

The evaluation was conducted with three expert instructors—a professor and two teaching assistants—across three MOOCs in CourseMapper: Learning Analytics, Human-Computer Interaction, and Web Technologies. The user scenario centers on university learners in MOOCs, indicating an undergraduate context, while the actual evaluators were educators rather than students. Instructors reviewed the linguistic quality and relevance of generated questions and the perceived accuracy of answers.

The main conclusion is that the PKG-based question generation component showed strong promise for guiding learners toward relevant, personalized questions in context. Instructors rated the generated questions highly on fluency, clarity, conciseness, and relevance. However, the EduKG-based question answering component was less successful, with only 45% weighted average perceived accuracy across evaluated responses. The authors conclude that Graph RAG has potential to support personalized concept understanding in MOOCs, but that the answer generation component requires further improvement, including richer knowledge sources and better reasoning over retrieved evidence.

identified_tools.name: CourseMapper
identified_tools.description: A MOOC platform that incorporates Educational Knowledge Graphs (EduKGs), Personal Knowledge Graphs (PKGs), and a Graph RAG pipeline to recommend personalized questions and answer learner-selected questions about course concepts.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as the host platform implementing two AI-supported features: PKG-based question generation for learner-marked 'Did Not Understand' concepts, and EduKG-based question answering with citations drawn from Wikipedia-based graph retrieval.

findings.finding_summary: In expert evaluation across three MOOCs, the PKG-based question generation feature in CourseMapper received high ratings on linguistic quality and relevance. Weighted average scores on a 1–3 scale were Fluency=2.981, Clarity=2.835, Conciseness=2.973, Relevance to slide=2.853, and Relevance to DNU concept=2.668, based on evaluations of 100 question-answer pairs tied to 20 DNU concepts by 3 instructors.
findings.measure: Expert ratings of generated-question linguistic quality and relevance on 1–3 scales (Fluency, Clarity, Conciseness, Relevance to slide, Relevance to DNU concept)

findings.finding_summary: The EduKG-based question answering feature achieved 45.00% perceived accuracy overall in instructor review, with 45 correct answers out of 100. Accuracy varied by MOOC: Learning Analytics 56.67% (17/30), Human-Computer Interaction 45.00% (18/40), and Web Technologies 33.33% (10/30), with instructors noting many answers were too abstract or not sufficiently disambiguated.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI GPT-family large language models used for generating and answering natural-language educational questions.
identified_tools.use_case: A GPT-3.5-turbo model was used inside the Graph RAG pipeline for zero-shot PKG-based question generation and extractive question answering over graph-retrieved Wikipedia contexts.

findings.finding_summary: When GPT-3.5-turbo was used for PKG-based question generation within the Graph RAG workflow, expert instructors rated the generated questions highly on linguistic quality and relevance. Weighted averages on a 1–3 scale were Fluency=2.981, Clarity=2.835, Conciseness=2.973, Relevance to slide=2.853, and Relevance to DNU concept=2.668 across 100 evaluated question-answer pairs.
findings.measure: Expert ratings of generated-question linguistic quality and relevance on 1–3 scales

findings.finding_summary: When GPT-3.5-turbo was used for EduKG-based extractive question answering, overall perceived answer accuracy was 45.00% (45/100) in expert review. The paper reports that answers were often judged too abstract or incorrectly matched due to retrieval/disambiguation issues, despite citation support.

quality_tier_rationale: The paper reports an empirical evaluation, but it is a small expert-based human evaluation with 3 instructors rather than an RCT or quasi-experimental study with learners. Outcomes are perceptual ratings and judged accuracy, so the evidence is exploratory/mixed-methods in strength.
impact_tier_rationale: Results suggest promising question-generation quality but only moderate and inconsistent question-answering accuracy, with no standardized learner outcome effect sizes reported. Overall impact is therefore positive but unclear in magnitude.
